question: What are Django class-based views and when do you prefer them over function-based views?
title: Django Class-Based Views vs Function-Based Views
direct_answer: Class-based views (CBVs) use classes with HTTP method handlers (get(), post(), put()). Generic CBVs like ListView, DetailView, CreateView, UpdateView, DeleteView auto-generate common CRUD patterns. FBVs are simpler — one function, explicit flow. CBVs win for CRUD endpoints where the generic views reduce boilerplate. FBVs win for complex logic, custom authentication flows, and anywhere the CBV mixin stack becomes harder to follow than explicit code. APIView/ViewSets in DRF are the primary CBV pattern for REST APIs.
interviewer_intent: Tests practical Django experience — knowing when CBVs reduce boilerplate vs when they add complexity.

sections.title: CBV mechanics and tradeoffs
sections.content:
CBVs dispatch HTTP methods to class methods: a GET request calls get(self, request), POST calls post(). The as_view() class method creates the callable for urls.py.

Generic CBVs: ListView (GET list of objects), DetailView (GET one object), CreateView (GET shows form, POST creates), UpdateView, DeleteView. These read your model and form from class attributes and generate views automatically. For simple CRUD, this is dramatically less code.

Mixin composition: Django CBVs use multiple inheritance. LoginRequiredMixin, PermissionRequiredMixin, SuccessMessageMixin can be mixed in. The mixin stack is powerful but the MRO and attribute override mechanics require understanding Python's MRO.

When to use FBVs: when business logic doesn't fit the generic template, when you need explicit control over the flow, when debugging would require tracing through 5 mixin layers. FBVs are more readable for custom logic. When to use CBVs: standard CRUD, RESTful APIs with DRF's APIView/ViewSets.

sections.title: FBV vs CBV comparison
FBV vs CBV guide
items: Generic CBVs: ListView, DetailView, CreateView, UpdateView, DeleteView
CBVs win for standard CRUD — less boilerplate, more Django conventions
FBVs win for custom logic — explicit flow easier to debug
DRF: APIView for per-method control; ViewSet+Router for full CRUD

seo.metaTitle: Django Class-Based Views vs Function-Based Views — When to Use Each
seo.metaDescription: Compare Django CBVs and FBVs: generic ListView/DetailView/UpdateView, mixin composition, LoginRequiredMixin, and when to choose function-based views.

speakable_v2.hook: CBVs are a trade: less code for standard CRUD, more indirection for custom logic. Knowing when to use which separates productive Django developers.

beats.content: For standard CRUD — list, detail, create, update, delete — generic CBVs are significantly less code. class ArticleUpdateView(LoginRequiredMixin, UpdateView): with a few attributes replaces 20 lines of a function-based view.
For complex logic — multi-step workflows, custom auth, non-standard form handling — FBVs are more readable. You can trace the code top to bottom without understanding 5 mixin layers.

In DRF, APIView gives per-method control. ViewSet with a Router generates all CRUD URLs automatically. For REST APIs, ViewSet is the CBV equivalent of generic CBVs — minimal boilerplate for standard operations.

speakable_v2.cap: The CBV mixin stack is powerful but can be hard to debug. If you're pasting 'how does Django find get_queryset' into Google, the FBV is probably clearer for that view.
speakable_v2.followup_handoff: Follow up with DRF ViewSet vs APIView trade-offs, or Django's get_object_or_404 and permission checking patterns.
